name: Cotswolds
title: Holidays in the Cotswolds
intro: Honey-coloured stone villages, rolling hills, thatched cottages and country pubs, two hours from London. Here's what the Cotswolds are like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The stone cottages of Arlington Row in Bibury, a village in the Cotswolds

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: No passport checks within the UK

facts_note: UK and Irish citizens don't need a passport to travel within the UK, but airlines ask for photo ID. Most other visitors need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA), so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June and September are the best months, with gardens in bloom and pleasant walking weather. July and August are warm, but Bourton-on-the-Water, Bibury and Castle Combe get crowded with coaches, so arrive early. October has autumn colour, and December is cosy, with log fires and Christmas markets. Winter is cold and quiet.

things.name: Bourton-on-the-Water
things.blurb: The 'Venice of the Cotswolds', with low stone bridges over the River Windrush and a model village.

things.name: Bibury
things.blurb: Arlington Row, a lane of 17th-century weavers' cottages, is one of England's most photographed streets.

things.name: Broadway Tower
things.blurb: A folly on a hilltop with views over sixteen counties, and red deer in the park around it.

things.name: Blenheim Palace
things.blurb: Churchill's birthplace, with a huge palace, gardens, a maze and an adventure playground.

things.name: Cotswold Way
things.blurb: Walk a section of the 102-mile trail between Chipping Campden and Bath.

things.name: Cotswold Farm Park
things.blurb: Rare breeds, tractor rides and lamb feeding, run by Adam Henson from BBC Countryfile.

faqs.question: What is the best base in the Cotswolds?
faqs.answer: Stow-on-the-Wold, Chipping Campden and Moreton-in-Marsh are central, with trains from London at Moreton. Cirencester and Burford suit the southern villages.

faqs.question: Do you need a car in the Cotswolds?
faqs.answer: Yes, really. Buses between villages are few, though you can reach Moreton-in-Marsh, Kingham and Stroud by train and walk or cycle from there.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in the Cotswolds?
faqs.answer: A weekend covers a handful of villages. Three or four days lets you add walks, Blenheim Palace or a day in Bath or Oxford.

faqs.question: Which are the prettiest Cotswold villages?
faqs.answer: Bibury, Castle Combe, Lower Slaughter, Bourton-on-the-Water, Snowshill and Painswick are the favourites.
